Description: One of the oldest and most famous temples, built in 1738 and dedicated primarily to Guanyin, blending Buddhist, Taoist, and folk beliefs. A major spiritual and cultural landmark, renowned for its intricate architecture and its role as a community gathering place through wars and earthquakes.

A historic Taiwanese folk temple founded in 1804, built by immigrants from Tongan, Fujian, and dedicated to protecting their community. Celebrated for its refined traditional architecture, the temple received the UNESCO Asia Pacific Heritage Award for Culture Heritage Conservation in 2003.

A Confucian temple originally built in 1879, reflecting traditional Fujian style architecture and dedicated to Confucius and classical learning. A key cultural landmark in Taipei, symbolizing Confucian values of education and ritual, and historically used for ceremonies across different eras of rule.

One of the most famous Mazu temples, originally established in 1591 and dedicated to Mazu, the Goddess of the Sea and protector of sailors and fishermen. Renowned for its elaborate traditional wood carvings and long religious history, the temple remains a major pilgrimage site and cultural landmark in Lukang.

A prominent Mazu temple built in 1757, serving as an important center of Taoist worship and community life in Songshan. Famous for its structure, ornate roof decorations, and its close association with the lively Raohe Street Night Market.

A historic Buddhist temple founded in 1773, originally known as Guanyin Temple and later relocated to Dazhi during the Japanese period. Designated a cultural heritage site of Taiwan, the temple reflects layered architectural influences and a long history of restoration and religious significance.

A major Taoist temple built in 1967 and dedicated to Lord Guan, the patron deity of businessmen, soldiers, and police officers. Widely known for its disciplined worship practices and for becoming the first temple in Taiwan to ban incense burning in 2014 to reduce air pollution.

A Chan Zen Buddhist temple established in 1911, affiliated with the Linji school and dedicated to Shakyamuni Buddha. Noted for its Song dynasty inspired architecture and its role in promoting Zen practice in Taiwan during the Japanese period and beyond.

A rare Japanese style Buddhist temple built in 1905 during the Japanese colonial era, associated with the Shingon sect and dedicated to Avalokiteshvara (Guanyin), the guardian spirit of hot springs. Distinguished by its wooden hall, curved pillars, and bell shaped windows, the temple offers a strong Edo period Japanese atmosphere unlike most traditional Taiwanese temples.

A major Taiwanese folk belief temple dedicated to Kai Zhang Sheng Wang, established in 1811 and long regarded as the religious center of the local communities of  Taoyuan. Prominently located in downtown Taoyuan, the temple is a designated municipal historic site and a cultural symbol of the district, known for its elaborate Qing era architectural details.

A major Mazu temple established in 1897, regarded as the center of Mazu worship in northern Taoyuan and home to the revered Taoyuan Mazu. Known locally as Nanmenzi Mazu Temple, it has been relocated and rebuilt multiple times due to disasters and urban development, remaining an important focal point of community faith.

A local Taiwanese folk belief temple dedicated to the Three Officials ,for example , Sanyuan Dadi: Heaven, Earth, and Water Officials, serving as an important center of community worship in Bade. Known for its role in traditional festivals and merit ceremonies, the temple reflects the everyday religious life of local residents in Taoyuan.

The oldest temple in Taoyuan City, founded in 1661 and dedicated to Marshal Xuantan, the Martial God of Wealth, brought by Ming loyalist soldiers. A municipally designated historic site, the temple is a major center for folk festivals and pilgrimages, reflecting over 300 years of local religious life.

A historic temple originally built in 1791 and dedicated to Lord Yimin, a Hakka ancestral hero, it was later expanded and renamed Baozhong Temple in 1857. An important religious and cultural center for the Hakka communities of Pingzhen, Zhongli, and Yangmei, known for its traditional architecture and annual Yimin festivals.

A Confucius temple founded in 1726 during the Qing Dynasty, featuring Zhangzhou style architecture and centered on the Dacheng Hall dedicated to Confucius. Designated a national historic site, it has long served as a major cultural and educational landmark in central Taiwan, closely linked to traditional academies and schools OF  the region .

A historic Mazu temple completed in 1738, serving as one of the most important centers of Mazu worship in Changhua. Designated as a historic building, the temple is notable for its layered architectural styles, combining traditional Fujian elements with later Japanese era influences.

A historic temple established in 1735 and dedicated to Guan Sheng Di Jun , at Lord Guan or Guan Yu, serving as a major site of martial deity worship in Changhua. Designated as a county level historical site, the temple combines long-standing religious traditions with local cultural functions and continues to be revered by worshippers.

A major landmark of Changhua featuring the Bagua Mountain Giant Buddha, a tall Shakyamuni Buddha statue that has 23 meter completed in 1961 and inspired by the Kamakura Buddha of Japan. Part of the Bagua Mountain National Scenic Area, the site combines religious symbolism with panoramic views, ecological exhibits, and walking trails.

A historic temple founded in 1817 by settlers from Tongan, Quanzhou, primarily dedicated to Baosheng Dadi, the guardian deity of medicine and health. Designated as a county level historic site, the temple is admired for its refined Jiaozhi pottery, classical painted doors, and traditional courtyard based architectural layout.

A historic Guanyin temple founded in 1747, once celebrated as one of the Eight Scenic Spots of Changhua under the name Tiger Rock Listening to Bamboo. Set amid bamboo forests and rocky cliffs, the site is both a county designated historic monument and a popular religious and hiking destination.

A well known beach with rare golden sand formed at the mouth of the Shuang River and opened to the public in nineteen seventy five. A popular summer destination famous for swimming seaside activities and hosting large outdoor music events that attract visitors from across Taiwan.

A scenic pebble beach facing the Pacific Ocean known for its wide open views and curved coastline that attracts many visitors each year. Originally named after a lake shaped like the Big Dipper the area became a beach after land changes during the Japanese period and remains a landmark of Hualien.

A long white sand beach on the north coast known for strong sea winds wide tidal flats and open coastal views. Formed by ancient volcanic activity the area became a popular bathing and sightseeing destination during the Japanese period and remains a major seaside attraction today.

A sandy coastal area in Sanzhi known for relaxed seaside scenery and beaches suitable for families and casual walks. Formerly a popular attraction during the Japanese period the area is now lined with ocean facing cafes and small guesthouses that create a calm holiday atmosphere.

A small calm sandy beach close to Taipei that is popular for swimming and relaxing trips from the city. Known for light colored sand and easy access it became more popular after a coastal road connected the area with Wanli.

A long sandy beach with shallow water near Tamsui that is popular for walking sunbathing and seaside views due to its close distance from Taipei. Easily reached by light rail transit the beach is open to visitors but swimming is forbidden and there are no shower facilities.

A large coastal beach park with golden sand stretching about three kilometers along the northeast coast and connecting toward Fulong Beach. Known for swimming fishing sand activities and open sea views the park is well equipped with showers restrooms parking and walking paths.

A famous coastal sightseeing area in Kaohsiung known for sea views mountain backdrops and beautiful sunsets along the Taiwan Strait. Located beside National Sun Yat sen University the area includes a black sand beach and historic landmarks that overlook the bay.

A well known white sand beach in Kenting National Park with clear water and a wide bay suitable for swimming and water sports. Popular with visitors for snorkeling surfing and seaside activities the area also offers nearby facilities and easy access from Kaohsiung.

A small sandy beach in Kenting with clear warm water and frequent sunshine offering a quieter alternative to nearby South Bay. Famous for the nearby Sail Rock coral formation the beach is popular for water sports sunbathing and relaxed seaside visits.

A world famous Taiwanese restaurant chain founded in nineteen fifty eight and best known for its freshly made xiaolongbao dumplings. Originating from a small Taipei shop the brand grew into an international symbol of Taiwanese cuisine recognized for precision consistency and quality.

A famous Taipei street food shop in Ximending known for serving flour rice noodles with rich broth and tender intestines. Popular with locals and visitors the shop represents classic Taiwanese snack culture and is often enjoyed while standing.
